findings.title: Unrelated change: cleanup ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: This PR is about annotation-cleanup deadlocks, but it also changes the cleanup ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute. The ticker drives srv.clean(), which runs every cleanup job (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, user invites, short URLs, query history) as well as annotation cleanup. The change is not mentioned in the description and is not needed for the deadlock fix. It multiplies the periodic DB load of all these jobs by ten and changes operator-visible behavior. If it was left in by accident (for example a debugging tweak), it must be reverted. If it is intended, it needs to be called out and justified.

findings.title: Routine per-batch progress logged at Error level, including full ID lists
findings.body: The new logging uses r.log.Error for routine progress: 'Annotations to clean by time' (with the full ids slice, up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries), 'cleaned annotations by time' (line 537), the matching 'by count' calls (lines 554 and 557), and 'Tags to clean' / 'cleaned tags' (lines 576 and 579). untilDoneOrCancelled always runs at least one batch, including the final empty one, so every cleanup cycle emits error-level entries even when nothing was deleted. A large cleanup dumps up to 32767 IDs per batch into the error log. The 'err' field is always nil at the first call. These look like debugging leftovers. They will flood error logs and alerting, and the problem is worse now that the job runs every minute. They should be Debug-level without the ID list, or removed.

findings.title: Quadratic string building of the SQLite ID list
findings.body: The SQLite branch builds the IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) inside a loop. Each iteration copies the whole accumulated string, so building a list of n IDs costs O(n^2) bytes copied and allocated. With the batch size used in the new 40003-annotation test (32767), the final string is roughly 200KB and the loop copies several GB per batch, repeated for every batch and every annotation type. Use strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt into a byte slice.

findings.title: One bind parameter per ID breaks large batch sizes on MySQL and PostgreSQL
findings.body: The non-SQLite branch sends one bind parameter per ID. Previously the batch size was a literal in the LIMIT clause and could be any value. MySQL prepared statements and the PostgreSQL wire protocol cap bind parameters at 65535 per statement. A configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above that now makes the DELETE fail on every cycle, and the diff adds no upper bound on the setting. The SQLite workaround only covers SQLite. Either cap the batch size or split the DELETE into statements of bounded parameter count.
